source.snippet: Many users run Ollama on a primary workstation alongside other heavy workloads like gaming, media playback, or 3D rendering. When a user suddenly needs 100% of their GPU resources, there is no way to free the VRAM without completely terminating the Ollama service, which permanently destroys any long-running generations that are currently processing.

problem_statement: Developers and power users running local LLMs via Ollama on their primary workstation cannot pause or yield GPU/VRAM to other demanding applications without killing active generation sessions entirely, forcing a choice between LLM work and other GPU-intensive tasks.
target_segment: AI developers, ML engineers, and technical power users running local LLMs on consumer or prosumer GPU workstations for development, testing, or research workflows
notes: Buyer signal is moderate: these are developers actively using Ollama in workflows, some in professional/research contexts. The pain is concrete and technical. Monetization angle: a GPU resource manager or Ollama companion app (paid tier) that enables stateful pause/resume of LLM generations. Hobbyist use mixed with professional use; signal_strength kept at 2 due to single feature request with no upvotes, though the underlying user class (dev workstation LLM runners) is growing rapidly.
